files.why_added: Provides a separate explicit native identity entrypoint without changing Supabase repository, providers or app flows.
Coordinates protected durable prepare/readback/send recovery, generation invalidation, explicit rotation and server versus local signout.
Supplies one-submission native HTTP with trusted TLS, no redirects/cookies and bounded uncompressed request/response bodies.
Defines a versioned application/origin/club-bound protected CAS journal preserving original challenge, verification and refresh material.
Enforces exact wire fields/types, canonical tokens, numeric scope, supporter-only identity and duplicate JSON rejection; errors and protected objects are redacted.
Requires independently accepted OS protection, durable atomic CAS, process-safe exclusivity and bounded replies; unavailable store is the production default.
Implements exact current native challenge 202, verify/session/refresh/revoke 200 contracts, explicit native headers and no automatic retry.
Exercises durable-before-send ordering, storage failure/unknown acknowledgement, restart recovery, deadlines, two controllers and every asynchronous identity publication fence.
Runs a portable Dart-only contract smoke without Flutter initialization, Supabase, a native channel or external network calls.
Provides synthetic wire fixtures and a clearly test-only in-memory store/mutex; its declared capabilities do not demonstrate OS protection.
Rejects invalid scope, tokens, response status/headers/fields, expired/future proof, duplicate keys and redirect/body/cancellation hazards.

risks_and_unverified_limits: No dedicated Android/iOS credential channel or production OS store exists in this batch. Test memory storage and mutex are not secure storage evidence. Existing checkout marker storage is never used for credentials.

Keystore/Keychain protection, backup exclusion, rollback/reinstall/key-loss policy, cross-process locking, engine destruction, physical-device lifecycle and passcode requirements remain to implement and validate.

An unreadable or lost-key OS vault cannot be reset by this controller. abandonPendingForFreshVerification requires a readable journal; explicit vault retirement and recovered-file retention need a separate governed policy.

Current Flutter Supabase auth, profile, anonymous identity, phone-change, admin-role and paid-membership flows remain selected. The new standalone controller is not wired into app UI or the membership composition; only an invalidation callback port is supplied.

Identity import, anonymous upgrade/linking, authenticated contact change/recovery, profile compatibility, notification unlink, staff migration and complete account erasure are outside this foundation and remain open.

Fixture responses derive from reviewed current local workers; no real Cloudflare ingress context, D1, rate limiter, DNS/TLS endpoint, WhatsApp delivery, native OS API or provider/device acceptance was performed.

Physical clock trust is not implemented. Local bounded checks allow at most5 seconds of future phone proof and reject expired access; recovery refuses clock rollback and age>=60 seconds. Real device/server clock behavior remains unverified.
Explicit abandon discards local recovery, makes no claim of server revocation, and may leave a previously issued server session active. It is never invoked on launch, timeout or read-only access.

Identity is a point-in-time server observation fenced within this controller. Cross-process identity-change notification and launch policy remain adapter/composition work; every protected membership operation still requires its separate server authority check.
Wire native HTTP uses normal platform TLS trust; actual network and transport runtime acceptance remain open. No provider or financial entitlement is granted by a supporter identity.
No original production readiness task is declared fully accepted by this report. All runtime selection, provenance/import, named approvals, hosted CI and governed release gates remain open.
